ontology.note: The semantic contract belongs to the ruleset, which declares its own output vocabulary and basis; do not infer one from this widget.

changes.description: A number Relate brings onto a table whose values are named by a column, such as statistic, is read as a number, as on any other table: a census share related onto the shares of three population models was unreadable. "%" is understood as a unit, percent.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists, and the Validation Lab checks this widget exhaustively rather than by sample -- check 23 enumerates the complete input space of all three bundled rulesets, 46 cells, reproducing every conclusion with an independent decision table and verifying the emitted receipt. That is evidence about the rulesets and about this widget's four stages; it does not certify the widget independently, and it says nothing about whether any threshold is right. 0.12.0: tests/seven-one-seven.browser.mjs (four cases by hand: 9 and -1 days, NoVerdict where onset or response is missing); Chromium. Experiment 207: tests/data-issues.test.mjs, tests/seven-one-seven-ontology.test.mjs, tests/ruleset-example.test.mjs. 0.13.0: tests/band-rules.test.mjs (labels, conditions, every age in exactly one band, refusals). 0.13.1: scripts/sentence-numbers.mjs finds every number in each step's sentence among its results, across every worked example; Validation Lab check 49 recomputes MERS's 7-1-7 verdicts from the source files. 0.13.2: tests/rule-editor.browser.mjs and the rule tests; Chromium. 0.13.3: The population example's comparison chain over shares built from the reference totals: the census share read, the difference computed for all 90 Rwandan rows, run in Node; no browser test yet.
